summary: Anthropic released Claude Opus 4.8, an incremental update to its flagship model that includes new agentic and effort-control features and a price cut for its fast inference mode.

mechanisms.reason: New 'dynamic workflows' feature runs hundreds of parallel subagents to autonomously complete large multi-step engineering and analysis tasks, extending agentic displacement of manual workflows.
mechanisms.quote: Claude can plan the work and then run hundreds of parallel subagents in a single session (and with Opus 4.8, the agents can run for even longer).

mechanisms.reason: Fast mode pricing for Opus 4.8 was cut to a third of its previous cost while running faster, directly lowering per-token serving cost for that mode.
mechanisms.quote: fast mode for Opus 4.8—where the model can work at 2.5\u00d7 the speed—is now three times cheaper than it was for previous models.

mechanisms.reason: Higher effort settings and long-running parallel agent sessions consume more tokens per task, and rate limits were raised to accommodate this increased usage.
mechanisms.quote: We have increased rate limits in Claude Code to accommodate the higher token usage of higher effort levels.

mechanisms.reason: The release shows incremental benchmark gains and a few first-of-kind results (e.g. Legal Agent Benchmark) but is explicitly described as a modest improvement rather than a step change.
mechanisms.quote: Users will find Opus 4.8 to be a modest but tangible improvement on its predecessor.
